analysis.summary: The source discusses the development of automated pull request (PR) reviewers using coding agents, emphasizing that while the AI model is important, the overall system architecture plays a more significant role in effectiveness.
keyFindings: Automated PR reviewers have been developed using coding agents.
The AI model used is important but constitutes a small part of the system.
System architecture is more critical than the AI model in building effective automated PR reviewers.
limitations: The source is a brief blog post and lacks detailed empirical evidence or evaluation metrics.
No information on the performance or accuracy of the automated PR reviewers is provided.
The claims are based on the author's experience and may not be generalizable.

claims.text: The AI part of automated PR reviewers is surprisingly small compared to the overall architecture.
claims.evidence: Author's experience building multiple versions of automated PR reviewers.

claims.text: The architecture matters more than the AI model in building effective automated PR reviewers.
claims.evidence: Author's observation from developing several versions of the system.

relevance: Relevant for research on AI-assisted software development tools.
Informative for studies on system design for automated code review.
analysis.intervention: Automated PR reviewers using coding agents
outcomes: Role of AI model versus system architecture
suggestedRelationships: System architecture influences the effectiveness of automated PR reviewers more than the AI model.
Experience-based insights can guide the design of AI-assisted code review tools.
